findings.reason: the plan's only population measure would report success while two of its named false-halted mechanisms remain live.
findings.text: the census's halted-row figures cannot detect the §3 or §4 mechanism: figure one counts only rows whose event records `process_alive: true`, while §3's own reproduction row (r-20261023T012524464845-a-plan-write-refuses-the-bucket, 12:25:51Z in the reckon stream) records `process_alive: false`; figure two counts rows followed by a `working` row "with no new attempt claim between them", while that row follows the resumed attempt's 12:15:01Z claim and is followed by a delivery, and §4's repair row (12:14:49Z) precedes that same claim — so both figures read zero whether or not those two mechanisms are fixed

findings.reason: the builder cannot tell whether it must produce the report it cannot yet measure, and without a separate path its negative control is unrecorded.
findings.text: the report and the negative control belong to a separately dispatched node ("A second, short node composes the report", and "Negative control: … recorded in the report"), yet this node's write paths include "the report as this node's evidence fragment", so one section assigns one artifact to two nodes and leaves this node's own control with no other record location

findings.reason: a node reading the opening sentence may treat the commit as already done and skip writing the module its own done-when requires.
findings.text: "The instrument behind §1 is committed and re-run" is false: §1 states "The census script is in the coordinator's scratch", and scripts/census/ holds only death_census.py, carryover_census.py and pace_replay.py
